big-agnes-copper-spur-hv-ul2: Loved for its roomy, freestanding design and good ventilation; some report failing zippers.
big-agnes-copper-spur-ul1: Liked for easy freestanding pitch and generous storage; a few accept the extra weight.
big-agnes-copper-spur-ul2: Praised for roomy space, even for tall hikers; some report condensation and a floor that wet out.
big-agnes-fly-creek-ul2: Known for being light and long-lasting; many find it tight inside for two or taller people.
big-agnes-rapide-sl-insulated: Praised for comfort, especially for side sleepers; a good number find it colder than rated.
big-agnes-tiger-wall-ul1: Liked as a light, easy-to-pitch solo tent that handles wind; few real complaints.
big-agnes-tiger-wall-ul2: Loved for being light, very roomy for one and easy to pitch; some report snagging zippers.
durston-kakwa-40: Liked for comfort and a light frame that moves weight to the hips; fit varies and some find it sore.
durston-kakwa-55: Praised for carrying heavy loads well while staying light; some find it does not fit and sweats.
durston-wapta-30: Rated for comfort and low weight for a frameless pack; some find the shoulder straps hurt.
durston-x-dome-1: Valued for being roomy, freestanding and solid in wind and rain; it is not the lightest solo tent.
durston-x-dome-2: Loved for its roomy interior and easy freestanding pitch; several report bent poles in gusts.
durston-x-mid-1: Praised for generous vestibules and storm performance; some bigger hikers find the sleeping area snug.
durston-x-mid-1-solid: Valued for warmth and wind protection in cool conditions; many find the solid inner stuffy in heat.
durston-x-mid-2: Loved for being very roomy and solid in wind and rain; many find the big footprint hard to place.
durston-x-mid-2-solid: Rated for storm, wind and cold protection in a roomy shelter; many find the footprint large.
durston-x-mid-pro-1: Liked for its roomy interior, headroom and tough build; some find the pitch fussy on uneven ground.
durston-x-mid-pro-2: Praised for being light, roomy and storm-worthy; many find the big footprint hard to place.
durston-x-mid-pro-2-plus: Enjoyed for generous space for two and a dog at low weight; many need a large flat site.
enlightened-equipment-enigma: Liked as light, packable and warm for many; a sizable group find it colder than rated.
enlightened-equipment-revelation: Known for being light and versatile; nearly as many find it colder than its rating.
gossamer-gear-kumo-36: Liked for surprising comfort and useful pockets for a frameless pack; some find it tiring on long days.
gossamer-gear-mariposa-60: Praised for being light and comfortable at a good price; some report thin fabric that tears.
gossamer-gear-the-one: Liked for a quick pitch, generous room and good value; many find condensation the main problem.
gossamer-gear-thinlight-foam-pad: Valued as a light add-on that protects an inflatable pad; some find it too thin alone.
hyperlite-mountain-gear-20-degree-quilt: Praised for real warmth near freezing and roomy room for side sleepers; a couple call it pricey.
hyperlite-mountain-gear-southwest: Known as tough and water resistant; many find the straps painful with heavier loads.
jetboil-minimo-cooking-system: Praised for fast boils and good simmer control; few real complaints.
katabatic-gear-alsek-22-f-quilt: Loved for real warmth and good build quality; cold sleepers sometimes got chilly.
katabatic-gear-flex-15-f-quilt: Praised for warmth well below freezing; a few cold sleepers were cold.
katabatic-gear-flex-22-f-quilt: Liked as warm, comfortable and well made; many find it drafty for restless sleepers.
katabatic-gear-flex-30-f-quilt: Valued for warmth and a pad attachment many call the best; a few found it more than needed.
katabatic-gear-palisade-30-f-quilt: Rated for warmth beyond its rating and few drafts; a minority were chilly near freezing.
katabatic-gear-sawatch-15-f-quilt: Loved for genuine warmth and a cut that limits drafts; some find it too warm for summer.
msr-pocketrocket-2: Known as tough and reliable with good simmer control; many find it weak in wind and cold.
msr-pocketrocket-deluxe: Liked as a small, fast-boiling stove that simmers well; several say the igniter failed early.
nemo-hornet-elite-osmo: Praised as light, durable and storm-worthy; few real complaints.
nemo-hornet-osmo: Liked for roominess for its weight and quick setup; many call the 1P tiny.
nemo-switchback: Liked as a comfortable foam pad with no leak risk; some find it bulky and firm for side sleeping.
nemo-tensor-all-season: Praised for comfort, warmth and a small packed size; some still feel cold.
nemo-tensor-elite: Loved for surprising comfort and a tiny packed size; many find it slippery and poorly insulated.
nemo-tensor-extreme-conditions: Valued for warmth and comfort in cold or snow; few real complaints.
osprey-exos-48: Praised for comfort up to moderate loads and excellent back airflow; some find the hip pockets awkward.
osprey-exos-58: Liked for comfort and a mesh back that keeps sweat down; some find comfort fades past 30 pounds.
platypus-gravityworks: Valued for filtering plenty of water quickly for groups; many find it clogs or flows slowly.
platypus-quickdraw: Loved for fast flow and easy backflushing; some report dud units or poor flow.
sawyer-squeeze: Known as long-lived and easy to backflush; many find it slows or clogs after storage.
sea-to-summit-ether-light-xr: Loved for comfort, especially for side sleepers, and small packing; some find it noisy.
sea-to-summit-spark-pro: Liked for an open footbox and zips that let them vent; some find it roomy.
six-moon-designs-gatewood-cape: Prized as a very light shelter that doubles as a poncho; many find condensation a problem.
six-moon-designs-lunar-solo: Liked as roomy, light and easy to pitch once learned; many find condensation the main complaint.
soto-amicus: Valued as compact, sturdy and good value; a few say the igniter failed.
soto-windmaster: Praised for fuel efficiency and strength in wind; many find the igniter fails, so carry a lighter.
tarptent-aeon-li: Liked as very light and easy to pitch with a small footprint; some find it snug for taller hikers.
tarptent-double-rainbow-li: Loved for generous room, light weight and easy pitch; many find condensation the main complaint.
therm-a-rest-neoair-xlite-nxt: Praised for warmth for the weight; several report leaks or valve trouble.
therm-a-rest-neoair-xtherm-nxt: Loved for great warmth for its weight, even on snow; several side sleepers got hip pressure.
therm-a-rest-z-lite-sol: Valued as a tough foam pad that cannot be punctured; many find it firm and sore for side sleepers.
toaks-titanium-750ml-pot: Liked for fitting a small stove and canister inside; a few find it narrow with uneven heating.
ula-circuit: Praised for durability and comfort at moderate loads; many find comfort fades past 30 pounds.
western-mountaineering-alpinlite: Valued for reliable warmth and an accurate rating; many find it heavy compared with quilts.
western-mountaineering-astralite-top-qui: Praised for warmth for its weight and good build; some find the cut narrow and drafty.
western-mountaineering-megalite: Loved for warmth, a roomy cut and long life; one found it comfortable only to freezing.
western-mountaineering-summerlite: Liked as light, small and durable for three seasons; several say it feels like a 40F bag.
western-mountaineering-terralite: Liked as roomy and warm, especially for side sleepers; some find it heavy.
western-mountaineering-ultralite: Praised for warmth for its weight and good build; a few cold sleepers found it overhyped.
western-mountaineering-versalite: Loved for warmth and good build, especially by cold sleepers; a few found it overkill.
zpacks-arc-haul-ultra: Praised for comfort and ventilation at a light weight; some report durability problems.
